records.text: Tyler Robinson ate at Cowboy Smokehouse in Panguitch on the evening of September 10.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: he was alone. And what we can tell you that he did when he got there was that he pulled into Cowboys Smokehouse on North Main Street. He grabbed himself a seat at the bar at this steakhouse, and he ordered himself some more food.

verification.notes: Restaurant staff reported that a quiet customer resembling Robinson ate there that night, but neither law enforcement nor public payment records conclusively identify the customer as Robinson.

records.text: A Cowboy Smokehouse server recognized Tyler Robinson from news photos, and management verified his visit through a credit-card receipt.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Well, one of the servers recognized him as the person that was sitting at the bar the night before. So they decided to huddle up with management and said, no, that that person, Tyler Robinson, he was here. ... what they decided to do was to verify that he was in the building. ... but rather just looking through credit card charges.

verification.notes: Independent reporting confirms staff recognized a customer as resembling Robinson and the restaurant reported the lead. Public records do not confirm that a credit-card charge identified Robinson, so the compound claim is only partly supported.

sources.title: One of Tyler Robinson’s last meals as a free man may have been a steak dinner — medium rare
sources.relevance: Reports that restaurant staff recognized a customer matching Robinson from news photos and located a receipt, but does not independently confirm the card belonged to Robinson.

records.text: Federal investigators did not visit Cowboy Smokehouse to interview staff or investigate Tyler Robinson's reported visit.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I would expect that they would have gone down to this restaurant. I can tell you guys today they have not. Nobody is interested in coming down to this restaurant and speaking with these employees

verification.notes: No public law-enforcement record establishes whether investigators had visited or interviewed the restaurant staff by the episode's January 6 publication date. Later reports describe subsequent contacts but do not resolve the timing.

records.text: The FBI possesses the Cowboy Smokehouse receipt documenting Tyler Robinson's visit.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I have confirmed that that happened; again, there was a literal receipt and the FBI knows about it and has that in their possession

verification.notes: No FBI release or independently authenticated record confirms FBI possession of a receipt tied to Robinson. A later circulated receipt has a blurred card number and remains unauthenticated.

records.text: Tyler Robinson arrived at Cowboy Smokehouse at approximately 8:45 p.m. and left around 9:30 p.m.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And now we can add that 8.45 p.m. That's the time, approximately, that Tyler (Tyler Robinson) turned up in Panguitch, Utah. Again, that is three hours away from Orem. He has a meal at the bar counter, and then he leaves around 9.30 p.m.

verification.notes: Staff later described an approximately 8:45 p.m. sighting, but a circulated receipt shows about 8:55 p.m. to 9:47 p.m., and the customer's identity remains unconfirmed.

sources.title: One of Tyler Robinson’s last meals as a free man may have been a steak dinner — medium rare
sources.relevance: Reports the staff’s recollection of the customer and visit while stopping short of conclusively identifying the customer as Robinson.

sources.title: Cowboy’s Smokehouse Receipt
sources.relevance: Documents the circulated receipt’s 8:55 p.m. order and 9:47 p.m. payment times and explains that the receipt and payment-card identity remain unauthenticated.

records.text: Wilson said he received hundreds of messages from people who did not know the steakhouse receipt was a complete fraud.
records.speaker: Andrew Wilson

appearances.snippet: I got hundreds of DMs, for instance, from people who didn't know that the steakhouse receipt was a complete phony fraud, that the whole thing is a fraud.

verification.notes: The underlying program transcript directly records Wilson saying he received hundreds of direct messages from people who did not know what he called the steakhouse receipt's 'complete phony fraud.' This verifies the attributed statement. The number and content of private messages cannot be independently counted, and 'fraud' was Wilson's characterization rather than an adjudicated finding.

sources.title: The Stuff That Has To Be Said: Live Special with Andrew Wilson — Transcript
sources.relevance: Directly reproduces Wilson's hundreds-of-DMs statement and his characterization of the receipt.

records.text: Owens said the FBI knew of the Panguitch restaurant lead and took a statement from the owner; she also said she spoke to the owner, the server gave an interview, and a debit-card receipt existed.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I don't know how many times I can say this. I guess I'm going to basically say to them what I said to Andrew face to face is you can keep saying this. You're going to eventually embarrass yourself. As I said, they got in touch with the FBI. ... The FBI is aware of this. The FBI took a statement from the owner. I spoke to the. ... But I spoke to the owner. The server has given an interview. There is a receipt. ... this was found this Panguitch thing was actually found by podcasters podcasters who were investigating stumbled upon this and like i said the fbi was contacted there is a report made it happened

verification.notes: Current on-location citizen reporting publishes a receipt, a recorded owner interview, and a recorded server interview. The owner says he gave the FBI everything he had, and staff describe contacting the FBI; the receipt is a debit transaction but contains no customer name and has not been authenticated by a court. These sources support that a restaurant lead, server interview, and debit receipt exist, but there is no public official FBI confirmation that it took the owner's statement, and Owens' own conversation with the owner is not independently documented.

sources.title: Panguitch — The Town That Breaks the Timeline
sources.relevance: Collects the current receipt image, raw owner and server interviews, and clearly notes the evidence is unauthenticated and not a court finding.

sources.title: Candace Owens vs. Andrew Wilson: The Charlie Kirk Debate
sources.relevance: Records Owens' account that she spoke to the owner and understood a receipt existed, while acknowledging limits in tying it to Robinson.

records.text: Owens acknowledged that the restaurant server could sincerely have believed they saw Tyler Robinson and still have misidentified him.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: i'm so sorry you guys but it happened now is it possible if they weren't being absurd they would just say okay yeah i hear you but candace is it possible that the server just misidentified him And then I'd say, yeah, ... of course, there's always a possibility that people truly believe that they see someone a la Mitch Snow. We did the Fort Huachuca thing.

records.text: Owens alleged that Andrew Wilson had been sent to elicit defamatory clips for a lawsuit, defend Israel and Erika Kirk, and press her to remove the Panguitch restaurant visit from her timeline; she did not identify who allegedly sent him.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I want to talk to you about this Panguitch receipt. So Andrew Wilson, when he came here, obviously was not sent to bait me on the evidence in the case. That's why he lost so brutally. ... He was sent to try to entrap me in a lawsuit to be out of context clips, trying to get me to say something defamatory on record. ... He was also sent to defend Israel and Erika (Erika Kirk) because that seems to go hand in hand. And lastly, and most obscurely, to demand that I remove. ... The Panguitch steakhouse visit from our official timeline. He was really up in arms about that official timeline.

records.text: Owens said citizen journalist Diligent Denizen interviewed a Cowboy Smokehouse waiter and released the restaurant receipt.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Then there was a journalist, a citizen journalist who goes by diligent denizen who dropped an interview with one of the waiters that was working that night. ... And he then released a receipt to go along with it because people were saying that he was lying and he was making it up.

records.text: Owens said the restaurant receipt was real and had been verified, while acknowledging she was unsure whether Diligent Denizen had worked with the owner.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: When I first saw this, I assumed that he was working with the owner because people were essentially calling the owner a liar. ... That may not have been the circumstance. I'm not sure the receipt, of course, has been verified. It is real. ... Here is the receipt. And it was met with a bunch of people then insisting at various times that the receipt was fake, that the receipt was non-existent, that the story had somehow been debunked, that people were lying, lying about what exactly.

records.text: Owens said the Cowboy Smokehouse owner had not been present that night; servers reported believing they had served Robinson, and the owner contacted the FBI before the receipt was retrieved.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Obviously i'm not the only person that he spoke to and he didn't claim to be there that night he basically told the story he was just responsible a responsible character your servers come to you and say i served this man last night i'm certain it was him he contacted the fbi at that time and they then pulled this receipt

records.text: Owens said the restaurant had apparently received harassment and negative reviews since July and guessed that people she called "Fed sloppers" were responsible; she said she did not know the source.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Apparently, since July, they have been severely harassed out of nowhere. People writing bad reviews of the restaurant, I mean, completely psychotic, don't know where that's coming from. ... My guess would be it would be the Fed sloppers doing that because they wanted this story to go away.

records.text: Owens rejected Andrew Wilson’s argument that the electronic signature on the restaurant receipt disproved Robinson’s involvement, arguing that an electronic scribble was not sufficient to establish who paid.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Andrew Wilson drops this signature as a debunking. This is a signature that was pulled and says, well, this is not Tyler Robinson's signature, so we can all move on from the idea that Tyler Robinson was at the steakhouse. That is completely and utterly wrong. ... First and foremost, people that pointed out that this is your standard when you get those like CVS electronic signature things. ... I draw on those things. I mean, I don't even kind of sign my name because it's so difficult to sign on them. Like, so I just thought this just looks like scribble to me, just literal basic scribble that we've all done. You do something to the driver's license scribble because it's just hard to actually write on these things. ... But I first want to tell you why this really matters before I softly try to suggest to you what I have learned.

records.text: Owens argued conditionally that a confirmed 9:47 p.m. Panguitch departure would conflict with Robinson’s claimed late-night presence in Orem. She stated an earliest 1:47 a.m. arrival despite describing a three-hour drive, then conceded he could have lied in texts about being on campus.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Panguitch is a three-hour drive away from UVU campus, okay? I mean, we're talking, it's just a three-hour drive. There's no way around it. ... You will recall that Tyler's messages to Lance (Lance Twiggs) that evening put him in Orem by 11, 11.45 p.m., okay? ... He also texts Lance (Lance Twiggs) that he was at UVU around 9 p.m. when he saw the canines, but the steakhouse receipt, if it's verified, would mean. ... That he didn't leave the steakhouse until about 9.47 p.m. earliest. That makes all of those late night text messages impossible. ... OK, so that's why this deeply matters. If it is proven that he was at the Cowboy Smokehouse, then Tyler Robinson would not have been able to make it back up to Orem. ... Until 1 47 a.m the earliest i'm going to reiterate that for you because it's very important if the steakhouse receipt is confirmed it removes any possibility that the text messages were sent from tyler robinson okay unless i guess you could say he was just lying and pretending he was on campus it's i guess it doesn't remove every possibility

records.text: Owens argued that if the steakhouse receipt established Robinson’s presence there, he could not have driven the car in the 12:36 a.m. Goforth stop; this relied on her disputed travel-time inference.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: If the steakhouse receipt is confirmed, Tyler could not be behind the wheel driving his car when it is stopped by Officer Goforth at 1236 a.m. He wouldn't have been able to make it back in time.

records.text: Owens said her initial confidence that the receipt belonged to Robinson was about 60 percent and acknowledged that sincere servers could have misidentified someone and that the account might be debunked at trial.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So I'm going to say that when we first looked into this story and after I spoke to the owner, I was probably personally at like a 60 percent chance that the receipt might have belonged to Tyler Robinson. We obviously did our best to verify it. ... The owner, like I said, was very forthcoming with what he knew. He wasn't like this was 100 percent him. It just this is what happened. But again, we we have that we had that blind spot, which is this relies on the memory of the server. ... Right. Or the servers. It doesn't necessarily make it true. They could be telling the truth and they think they saw this person, but it could be somebody else. ... And that's why I was we put it on our official timeline because we did our due diligence, but we certainly would have never said that we were 100 percent sure we were open to the possibility that as we got through the trial, this could be debunked and it could have just been a case of misremembering. Same thing.

records.text: Owens raised her stated confidence from 60 to 95 percent that the card used at Cowboy Smokehouse belonged to Tyler Robinson, citing unnamed sources, while explicitly allowing that someone else might have used his card.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: What I can tell you now is that after going to my sources, I am now moving myself from a 60%, which was where I was at, to a 95% certainty that it was Tyler Robinson's debit card that was swiped at the Cowboy Smokehouse on that night. ... Okay. I'm at a 95% certainty with what I know and what I am going to suggest will come out during this trial, that it was Tyler Robinson's card that was swiped at the Cowboy Smokehouse on that night. ... Now, did somebody else have his credit card? It's possible. Of course it's possible. Was somebody dressed like him, looked like him, but had his credit card? ... That's a possibility I'm open to. ... But I'm, again, going to stress that I'm of 95% certainty that the card that was used belonged to Tyler Robinson.
